title: Entra ID ↔ Google Cloud Identity — SSO Federation & Provisioning (GCDS / SCIM)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (Google Workspace + Gemini enterprise transformation; architecture/governance/integration or migration work, live-environment care).

Google Admin console + Microsoft/Entra authored click-by-click from public docs; Gemini Enterprise preview/rolling-out capabilities cited or flagged 'verify in tenant', never invented; third-party migration-tool and enterprise-app internals deferred to vendor docs.
hook: One identity across Microsoft and Google
problem: In a Google transformation, identity is the backbone: users must sign in once and exist consistently across both clouds. This solution federates Microsoft Entra ID with Google Cloud Identity for SSO and stands up provisioning (Google Cloud Directory Sync / SCIM) so accounts, groups, and licensing stay consistent — the identity foundation for coexistence and migration, deployed pilot-first and rollback-ready.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the identity model: Entra ID as IdP federating to Google (SAML/OIDC), provisioning via GCDS or SCIM, and how source-of-truth flows.
Requirements Guide — prerequisites (Entra ID + Google super-admin, source of truth, GCDS host or SCIM, DNS, a pilot) with how to verify/implement each.
Implementation Guide — exact steps to configure Entra→Google SSO federation, set up GCDS/SCIM provisioning of users+groups, validate sign-in and provisioning on a named pilot, then expand.
5 supporting scripts — identity-readiness discovery, per-user SSO + provisioning validation, an identity coverage/exception report, safe remediation, and a scope helper.
Testing & Troubleshooting Guides (SSO works, users/groups provisioned, licensing correct) plus Best Practices for source-of-truth and lifecycle.
short: Federate Entra ID with Google Cloud Identity for SSO and stand up provisioning (GCDS/SCIM) — consistent accounts, groups, and licensing across both clouds — the identity foundation for the transformation, pilot-first. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.
